taskVersion.name: deadline-math-hard-reasoned
taskVersion.description: Exploratory hard set, reasoning allowed. Convert deadlines to the reader's local time: relative dates, durations across a clock change, Unix and ISO timestamps, described dates, a traveling reader. Ground truth from zoneinfo.

parts.text:
I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Today is Saturday, October 24, 2026. Submissions close six days from today, on Friday, at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

To find the deadline in Madrid, Spain, we convert the Pacific Time (PT) deadline to Central European Time (CET):

1. **Date and Time of Deadline in PT:** 
   Six days from Saturday, October 24, 2026, is **Friday, October 30, 2026, at 11:59 PM PT** (23:59).

2. **Time Zone Offset for Pacific Time (PT):**
   In the US, Daylight Saving Time ends on the first Sunday of November (November 1, 2026). Therefore, on October 30, 2026, Pacific Time is still in PDT (UTC-7).

3. **Time Zone Offset for Madrid, Spain:**
   In Europe, Daylight Saving Time ends on the last Sunday of October (October 25, 2026). Therefore, on October 30, 2026, Madrid will already have switched to Central European Time (CET, UTC+1).

4. **Time Conversion:**
   - 23:59 PDT (UTC-7) on October 30 = 06:59 UTC on October 31.
   - 06:59 UTC + 1 hour = **07:59 CET on October 31, 2026**.

ANSWER: 2026-10-31 07:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Today is Friday, October 30, 2026. The form closes this coming Monday at 10:00 AM Los Angeles time."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

To find your local deadline in Madrid, Spain (Central European Time):

1. **Target Date:** "This coming Monday" after Friday, October 30, 2026, is **Monday, November 2, 2026**.
2. **Los Angeles Time Zone:** Daylight Saving Time in the US ends on Sunday, November 1, 2026. Thus, on Monday, November 2, Los Angeles will be in Pacific Standard Time (PST, UTC-8). 
3. **Madrid Time Zone:** Daylight Saving Time in Europe ends on Sunday, October 25, 2026. Thus, on Monday, November 2, Madrid will be in Central European Time (CET, UTC+1).
4. **Time Difference:** Madrid (UTC+1) is **9 hours ahead** of Los Angeles (UTC-8).
5. **Conversion:** 10:00 AM PST + 9 hours = 19:00 (7:00 PM) CET on the same day.

ANSWER: 2026-11-02 19:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The hackathon starts Saturday, October 24, 2026 at 18:00 Madrid time and lasts exactly 48 hours."
When is the end of the hackathon in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The hackathon begins on Saturday, October 24, 2026, at 18:00 CEST (UTC+2), which corresponds to 16:00 UTC. 

Adding exactly 48 hours brings the end time to Monday, October 26, 2026, at 16:00 UTC. 

In Spain, Daylight Saving Time ends on the last Sunday of October (October 25, 2026), at which point clocks move back 1 hour from CEST (UTC+2) to CET (UTC+1). Therefore, on Monday, October 26, Madrid local time is CET (UTC+1). Converting 16:00 UTC to local time yields 17:00 CET.

ANSWER: 2026-10-26 17:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The final round starts October 26, 2026 at 10:00 AM PT; submissions close exactly 72 hours later."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

To determine the deadline in Madrid local time:

1. **Calculate the deadline in PT:**  
   The contest starts on October 26, 2026, at 10:00 AM PT. Submissions close 72 hours (3 days) later, which is **October 29, 2026, at 10:00 AM PT**.

2. **Determine the time zones on October 29, 2026:**
   * **Pacific Time (PT):** Daylight Saving Time in the US ends on the first Sunday in November (November 1, 2026). Therefore, on October 29, the US is still in Pacific Daylight Time (**PDT, UTC-7**).
   * **Madrid Time:** Daylight Saving Time in Europe ends on the last Sunday of October (October 25, 2026). Therefore, by October 29, Madrid has already switched to Central European Time (**CET, UTC+1**).

3. **Convert the deadline to Madrid time:**  
   The difference between UTC+1 and UTC-7 is **8 hours**.  
   Adding 8 hours to 10:00 AM PDT gives **18:00 (6:00 PM)** on October 29, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-10-29 18:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close October 31, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET. Results are announced exactly 36 hours after submissions close."
When is the results announcement in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

To determine the exact time of the results announcement in Madrid local time:

1. **Submissions Close Time**: October 31, 2026, at 11:59 PM ET (EDT, UTC-4, as Daylight Saving Time in the US ends on November 1, 2026).
   - In UTC: **November 1, 2026, at 03:59 UTC**.

2. **Results Announcement (36 hours later)**:
   - November 1, 2026, 03:59 UTC + 36 hours = **November 2, 2026, at 15:59 UTC**.

3. **Convert to Madrid Time**:
   - European Daylight Saving Time ends on October 25, 2026, so on November 2, Madrid is on Central European Time (CET, UTC+1).
   - 15:59 UTC + 1 hour = **16:59 CET**.

ANSWER: 2026-11-02 16:59

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Deadline (Unix timestamp, seconds): 1791788340."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

To convert the Unix timestamp `1791788340` to Tokyo local time (JST, UTC+9):

1. **Convert to UTC:**
   - $1791788340 \text{ seconds} = 20,738 \text{ days and } 25,140 \text{ seconds}$ since the Unix epoch (1970-01-01 00:00:00 UTC).
   - $20,738 \text{ days}$ corresponds to **2026-10-12**.
   - $25,140 \text{ seconds} = 6 \text{ hours and } 59 \text{ minutes}$.
   - So, the UTC time is **2026-10-12 06:59:00 UTC**.

2. **Convert UTC to JST (UTC+9):**
   - $06:59 + 9 \text{ hours} = 15:59$.
   - The date remains **2026-10-12**.

ANSWER: 2026-10-12 15:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Deadline: 2026-10-25T02:30:00Z."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The given deadline is `2026-10-25T02:30:00Z` (02:30 UTC on October 25, 2026). 

In Spain (Madrid), Daylight Saving Time ends on the last Sunday of October, which in 2026 falls precisely on October 25. The shift from UTC+2 (CEST) to UTC+1 (CET) occurs at 01:00 UTC (03:00 local time). Since 02:30 UTC is after this 01:00 UTC transition, Madrid will be on UTC+1 at that time. 

Adding 1 hour to 02:30 UTC gives 03:30 local time.

ANSWER: 2026-10-25 03:30

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close at 11:59 PM Pacific Time on the last Sunday of October 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

To determine the local deadline in Madrid, Spain, we follow these steps:

1. **Find the date of the last Sunday of October 2026:**
   October 31, 2026 is a Saturday, making Sunday, **October 25, 2026** the last Sunday of the month.

2. **Determine the Pacific Time offset:**
   In the United States, Daylight Saving Time ends on the first Sunday of November (November 1, 2026). Therefore, on October 25, Pacific Time is still in Daylight Saving Time (PDT, which is **UTC-7**).
   - 11:59 PM PDT on October 25, 2026 = **06:59 UTC on October 26, 2026**.

3. **Determine Madrid's time offset:**
   In Spain, Daylight Saving Time ends on the last Sunday of October (October 25, 2026 at 03:00 CEST, turning back to 02:00 CET). By Monday, October 26, Madrid is operating on Central European Time (CET, which is **UTC+1**).

4. **Convert UTC to Madrid local time:**
   - 06:59 UTC on October 26, 2026 + 1 hour = **07:59 CET on October 26, 2026**.

ANSWER: 2026-10-26 07:59

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Deadline: 12:00 noon Eastern Time on the day the US ends daylight saving time in 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

In the United States, Daylight Saving Time ends on the first Sunday in November, which falls on **November 1, 2026**. 

At 2:00 AM on that day, Eastern Time transitions from EDT (UTC-4) to EST (UTC-5). Therefore, by 12:00 noon on November 1, 2026, Eastern Time is **EST (UTC-5)**.

Lima, Peru observes Peru Time (PET), which is **UTC-5** year-round. Since both time zones are at UTC-5 at that time, 12:00 noon Eastern Time is identical to your local time in Lima.

ANSWER: 2026-11-01 12:00

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Deadline: December 31, 2026, 24:00 AoE."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

AoE (Anywhere on Earth) corresponds to the UTC-12 time zone. "December 31, 2026, 24:00 AoE" is equivalent to January 1, 2027, 00:00 AoE.

Tokyo, Japan is in Japan Standard Time (JST), which is UTC+9. Since JST is 21 hours ahead of AoE (UTC-12), adding 21 hours to January 1, 2027, 00:00 AoE gives January 1, 2027, 21:00 JST.

ANSWER: 2027-01-01 21:00

I live in Madrid, Spain, but that week I'm traveling in New York, USA, and I need New York time. A contest page says: "The deadline is 5:00 PM Sydney time on October 5, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

To find the deadline in your local time (New York / US Eastern Time):

1. **Sydney Time Zone:** Daylight Saving Time (AEDT, UTC+11) begins in Sydney on the first Sunday of October (October 4, 2026). Therefore, on October 5, 2026, Sydney is at UTC+11.
   - 5:00 PM (17:00) AEDT on October 5, 2026, corresponds to **06:00 UTC** on October 5, 2026.

2. **New York Time Zone:** New York is on Eastern Daylight Time (EDT, UTC-4) in October.
   - Subtracting 4 hours from 06:00 UTC gives **02:00 (2:00 AM)** on October 5, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-10-05 02:00
